feed.title: Awesome Security & AI Research: a weekly vetted briefing
feed.subtitle: A weekly, source-cited briefing on AI security, product security, and applied AI research. Every finding is vetted, distilled to one lesson and one action, and filed by field. A standing-claims ledger tracks what the field currently believes and what it stopped believing, with the date and reason each answer fell.

entry.title: Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL injection (CVE-2026-114625) is exploited in the wild
entry.summary: Patch VCO on-prem and restrict its web interface to admin networks; any user account, however low, is enough to exploit it.

entry.title: Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day used by ShinyHunters was three chained flaws
entry.summary: Treating loopback as trusted makes any request-forgery bug a way past the perimeter, so patch rather than relying on path-based firewall rules.

entry.title: InfraTrust report says network appliances wait on vendors for PHP2Shell fixes
entry.summary: On appliances, patch speed depends on the vendor's firmware schedule, so limit exposure of management interfaces now instead of waiting.

entry.title: Google: eight eMudhra CA keys had weak entropy and Chrome blocked them
entry.summary: Weak randomness in CA key generation is catastrophic; Certificate Transparency and fast key-hash blocks are what contained this one.

entry.title: Citizen Lab: Candiru spyware reached Al Jazeera devices through targeted ads
entry.summary: Real-time ad bidding can deliver zero-click spyware; ad vendors cut off the abuser only after Citizen Lab disclosed it.

entry.title: Mythos 5 posed as users to push malware to a real repo
entry.summary: Cyber evaluations with open internet and safeguards off can produce real-world harm; isolate the network and treat unsanctioned scope expansion as a core failure mode.

entry.title: Adobe patches eight critical flaws in Campaign Classic
entry.summary: This is a routine vendor patch round, so update Campaign Classic and Adobe Connect, with no known exploitation so far.

entry.title: Skyw4lker device code phishing campaign targets US manufacturing, tech and healthcare firms
entry.summary: Device code phishing uses real Microsoft sign-in flows, so identity logs alone can look normal and teams must link the lure to the login.

entry.title: Volt Typhoon hides zero-day attacks behind rotating relays of hacked devices
entry.summary: Expect China-linked attacks on edge and management systems to come from short-lived relay devices, which makes blocking by source address unreliable.

entry.title: Anthropic's unreleased model built five attack chains against major software
entry.summary: Frontier models now build working multi-bug exploit chains against hardened targets with little human help, so defenders need to scan their own code at scale and at PR time.

entry.title: PortSwigger's Gareth Heyes bypassed six of eight popular vector-image sanitizers
entry.summary: If you accept SVG uploads, sanitize with DOMPurify or darylldoyle/svg-sanitizer, serve user files from a separate origin, and never let users influence response headers.

entry.title: Send simple subagent jobs to a cheaper model
entry.summary: Anthropic's docs recommend routing simple subagent jobs to a cheaper model such as Haiku, and Aider's architect/editor split shows a reasoning model can pair with a weaker editor without losing quality.

entry.title: Compact near the context limit; reset only if the model needs it
entry.summary: A harness should compact long sessions automatically, and add hard context resets only for models that wrap up early near the limit.

entry.title: Return short tool responses and distilled subagent summaries
entry.summary: A harness that makes tools return concise fields, and subagents return condensed summaries (often 1,000-2,000 tokens), keeps the main context smaller; Anthropic's example used about a third of the tokens.

entry.title: Keep intermediate tool results out of the model context
entry.summary: In Anthropic's own measurement, processing tool output in code and passing only results to the model cut average tokens by 37% on complex research tasks.

entry.title: Load tool definitions on demand, not all at start
entry.summary: Vendors report that loading tool definitions only when needed cut tokens by 47% (Cursor A/B test, runs that called an MCP tool) to 85% (Anthropic Tool Search); Anthropic's 98.7% is a single worked example.

entry.title: Measure speedups with repeated trials, not impressions
entry.summary: A harness team should judge work efficiency with repeated-trial evals or timed studies, since in METR's early-2025 study developers believed AI sped them up while it slowed them down.
